- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” — keep forecast slightly above true for 1–2 periods.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a “smooth decay” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day from day 5 onward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment rises, forecast should rise; if sentiment falls, forecast should fall).
